blocks.text: You can configure SecureAuth SSO as the authentication method for the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform), allowing users to sign in through your SecureAuth SSO provider, instead of using a username and password. To do this, you can specify a domain, and users with email addresses matching that domain are redirected to authenticate through SecureAuth. Each user must have an account with the same email address in both the Agentic SecOps Platform and SecureAuth. After SSO is enabled for a domain, it becomes the only authentication method for the Agentic SecOps Platform.
To configure SecureAuth SSO, complete the following steps:

blocks.item: Step 1: Generate SAML Details
To set up SecureAuth SSO account authentication, you must generate a SAML Entity ID and Reply URL within the Agentic SecOps Platform. To learn more, see Generating SAML Details.
Step 2: Create an App Integration
To enable SAML-based authentication with SecureAuth, you need to create and configure a new app integration.
To create an app integration:
Log in to the SecureAuth Identity Platform.
In the left-side navigation, go to New Experience > SecureAuth IdP.
Click Application Manager.
See image.
Click Add an Application to open the application template library.
Select SAML Application from the library.
See image.
On the Applications Details page:
Application Name: Enter the Agentic SecOps Platform name.
Application Description: Enter a description for the application.
Upload: Upload a logo from your system.
Data Stores: Enter the data stores to authenticate and allow user access.
Groups: Enter the groups allowed to access the application.
You can also enable Allow users from every group in your selected data stores access to this application.
See image.
Click Continue.
The Connection Settings page appears.
On the Connection Settings page:
In the Configure Connection section:
Select SP Initiated from the Connection Type drop-down menu.
Select By Redirect.
See image.
In the User ID Mapping section:
User ID Profile Field: Select the relevant user ID from the drop-down menu.
Name ID Format: The format is selected by default.
See image.
In the SAML Assertion section:
​​IdP Issuer: Enter the entity ID from Step 1.
Assertion Consumer Service (ACS): Enter the Reply URL from Step 1.
SP Login URL: Enter the URL https://app.avalor.io?domain=<your domain>.
Assertion will be valid for: Select an appropriate value.
Encrypt SAML Assertion: Disable the toggle.
All the remaining settings should be set to default.
See image.
In the SAML Attributes section, click Add SAML Attribute:
Attribute Name: Enter the attribute name.
Data Store Property: Choose the value that represents the user's email (Email).
Namespace (1.1): Enter http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress.
See image.
Click Add Application.
The Information for Service Providers page appears.
See image.
Click Download Metadata. You will need this information for the next step.
Enter the SecureAuth IdP appliance URL or IP address as the domain name (e.g., https://secureauth.company.com or https://111.222.33.44).
See image.
Click Download to download the metadata.
Step 3: Share Metadata with Zscaler
After registering an app in the SecureAuth Identity Platform, share XML metadata with your Zscaler Account team.
To share metadata with Zscaler:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, and click Account Settings.
In the Authenticate section, paste the XML metadata into the SAML XML MetaData field.
If the Authenticate section is not visible, share the XML metadata with your Zscaler Account team.
See image.
While a metadata URL is also supported, Zscaler recommends pasting the XML metadata directly.
